problem_type: Paid confirmation cards hide price/output-affecting model parameters behind the overflow controls
symptom: The paid-card walkthrough could not find the real 尺寸 control for a pixel-size image model before the confirmation timeout.
direct_cause: The shared parameterControlRole function returned null for a non-ratio size alias, so splitPrimaryParameterControls sent that control to the overflow panel.
class_root: Parameter aliases were used by the de-duplication boundary but the primary-parameter role boundary only represented ratio-valued size aliases; the same catalog field therefore had no visible paid-card role when its values were pixels or resolution names.
affected_population: Built-in image and video model archetypes whose price/output controls use size, imageSize, videoSize, video_size, image_size, quality, resolution_type, mode, upscale_factor, or quantity aliases
Paid confirmation cards and the inline parameter bar that consume the shared primary-parameter split
entry_points: Model archetype parameter controls are normalized by parameterControlRole; the node composer reads the role for its quantity button and the panel de-duplicates aliases through the same roles (the paid card's primary-chip split is deleted, 2026-10-24).
internal_only_reason: This invariant is owned by Nomi's shared model-archetype role mapping and paid-card composition; no external dependency decides which catalog aliases are user-facing spend controls.
invariants: Every image/video catalog control that represents a priced or output-defining ratio, size, resolution/quality, duration, or output quantity is assigned its semantic role when it has a renderable value.
Aspect aliases are de-duplicated only when their options are actual aspect ratios; non-ratio size aliases remain independently visible as resolution controls.
No paid surface splits controls into visible and hidden: the paid card has no controls, and the node's panel shows every control except the quantity, which moves to the composer's quantity button.

door_reduction.why_not: One classifier (parameterControlRole) and its one reader outside its own file (the composer's quantity control); the paid-card chip splitter that also read it is deleted.

generality_proof: The role decision is centralized in parameterControlModel and read by the one composer; the paid card's chip splitter that also applied a visibility policy on top of it is deleted, so there is no second policy left to diverge.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Map model and catalog aliases to the user-facing semantic role while preserving option-aware aspect-ratio identity.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Reads the quantity role from parameterControlRole; the panel then omits that control (one home per value).
Alias de-duplication uses the same option-aware roles (parameterControlModel.test.ts).

recurrence.reason: The alias is reused across multiple providers and model generations, and the same key can carry ratio, pixel, or resolution values. A new archetype or another caller can reproduce the omission unless role classification remains centralized and catalog-wide tested.
same_class_scan: Enumerated MODEL_ARCHETYPES modes for every image/video profile and collected all parameter keys and labels.
Searched parameterControlRole, splitPrimaryParameterControls, InlineParameterBar, NodeGenerationComposer, and the three paid walkthroughs.
Checked the existing Agnes size/ratio regression and the pixel-size paid-card characterization before implementation.

prevention.invariant: Non-ratio size aliases always resolve to the resolution role; only option-confirmed ratio aliases resolve to aspect, and all other priced/output aliases resolve to their semantic role.
prevention.failure_mode: An unrecognized alias returns null and stays in the panel like any other control.
prevention.strategy: Keep classification and option-aware de-duplication at the shared control boundary; with the paid card carrying no controls there is no visibility policy left to apply on top of it.

legacy_paths.rationale: This fix changes the shared role classification in place; there is no obsolete persisted format or fallback implementation to migrate.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The failure is in Nomi's catalog-role invariant and does not depend on a third-party runtime behavior.

migration: No persisted data migration is needed. Existing size, ratio, quality, duration, and quantity values continue to use their existing keys; only their paid-card visibility role changes. 2026-10-24 D2 step 3 (design card docs/plan/2026-10-23-d2-pointer-spend-card.md; contract docs/fixes/2026-10-24-spend-card-one-engine.root-cause.json): the paid card became node pointers plus a read-only summary that hands its shots to the canvas engine; splitPrimaryParameterControls (the paid-card primary-chip split) was deleted with the old card, so this contract's boundaries, doors, tests and legacy paths were re-pointed to the code that holds the invariant today (problem, symptom, causes and class root above are the original record).
residual_risks: The real-catalog paid-card chip matrix (every priced/output control in the primary set) was retired with the chips on 2026-10-24; parameterControlModel.test.ts keeps the role and de-duplication cases.
Independent acceptance remains pending because this local implementation session is not the separate acceptance line.
